title_guess: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016: the six steps of the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP), who acts at each step, who may not bid, and the time limits
recurring_cast: law_document (green 'LAW' book icon with 'IBC Code' tag and the Code's full name, fixed top-left on every canvas after 27 s)
CIRP map: a blue panel with one horizontal line, six dots and six step chips, with a black ring that marks the current step
bank_building (the lender, always on the left)
brand_logo (round NCLT seal with the national emblem) and small 'NCLT' tags pinned to the dots where the tribunal acts
cream step chips that later fly to their place in the picture (Committee of Creditors, Insolvency professional)
factory (the defaulting company, framed in green once the process starts)
running_examples: a bank's 10 crore loan to a factory, tagged NPA, with the payback line crossed (on screen only, never spoken)
time limits: 14 days to accept or reject the application, 330 days for the whole process
recall curve: gross NPA 24.8% (1994) falling to 2.5% (2011) and 2.78% (March 2023), with earlier measures pinned on it (numbers never spoken)

best_moments.why: the whole six-step process appears first as one map; every later return to the map moves a black ring to the next dot, so the learner always sees where the current step sits in the whole
a bank lends '10 Cr' to a factory, the loan is tagged NPA and the dotted payback line back to the bank carries a red cross: default in one picture before any new term

the heading chips fly to their place: 'Insolvency professional' drops into a green frame round the factory (he runs the company), 'Committee of Creditors' drops beside the bank (the lenders): who acts on whom is shown by position
three potential investors each send a plan document along dotted arrows that converge on the Committee of Creditors under the bank: many plans, one chooser
recall of earlier measures is done by pinning each one at its year on the NPA curve, and today's topic is appended to the last pin
at the last dot a calendar-with-clock pops over the map and the limits are written beside it (330 days, then 14 days): the time rule is attached to the process it limits

weak_moments.why: the best story of the video (defaulting promoters coming back as bidders for their own company, stopped by a 2017 amendment) is told for about 27 s over a still bullet list; the only picture is a bullet that appears at 267 s
NCLT is explained by a five-line paragraph under its seal, read out almost as written
the ineligible bidders are a text bullet list; none of the five kinds is drawn

numbers on the recall curve (24.8%, 2.5%, 2.78% March 2023) are never spoken, and five acronyms (SARFAESI, 5/25, SDR, S4A, AQR) are named in about 15 s without meaning; 2.78% for March 2023 may need checking (RBI's reported gross NPA ratio for March 2023 was about 3.9%)
the appeal arrow goes to NCLAT, a High Court and the Supreme Court as equal choices; under the Code the usual route is NCLAT and then the Supreme Court, so the High Court icon needs checking
the note 'creditors can withdraw within 30 days' needs checking against the Code (withdrawal after admission is usually tied to a 90% creditor vote); it also appears about 5 s before it is spoken
an app-promotion banner slides over the bottom half of the map while the 14-day limit is being spoken

segments.teaches: recall: gross NPA rose to a peak in the 1990s, fell, then rose again; earlier measures (Narasimham Committee II 1997, SARFAESI 2002, 5/25 refinancing 2014, SDR 2015, S4A and AQR 2016) are placed on the curve, and IBC is added as today's topic

five person icons (one red) on a black 'Narasimham Committee II' banner over 1997
GNPA % against years 1994-2023, pink shaded area under a curve falling from 24.8% to 2.5% (2011) and rising in a hump to 2.78% (March 2023)
green dashed pins at years: SARFAESI 2002 below the axis, 5/25 refinancing 2014, SDR 2015, S4A & AQR 2016 above
'& IBC Code' appended to the 2016 pin

segments.notes: 6 change events; the curve was built in earlier videos and is reused here as a recall board. Every percentage is shown, none spoken. Transcript reads 'NPS' at 1 s, a recognition error for NPA.
segments.idea: IBC is the newest of several measures against bad loans; each measure sits at its year on the NPA curve
segments.shown_as: the GNPA curve from earlier videos stays on screen; as each earlier measure is named, a green dashed pin drops at its year (SARFAESI 2002, 5/25 refinancing 2014, SDR 2015, S4A and AQR 2016), and '& IBC Code' is written onto the last pin when today's topic is named

segments.teaches: IBC 2016 gives a step-by-step process to resolve bad loans, called CIRP; the six steps are shown at once as a map

elements.what: green law-book icon with 'IBC Code' tag and the Code's full name
'CIRP | Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process' heading strip

blue panel, one horizontal line with six dots; dashed stems to step chips alternating above and below (admission of application; committee of creditors + insolvency professional; invite resolution proposers; approval of resolution plan; monitoring implementation; closure)
black ring settling on the first dot

segments.notes: The map appears whole on the word 'CIRP' (38.8 s); the six chip labels are not read out here. The ring lands on dot 1 as 'first step' is said.
segments.idea: resolving an insolvent company follows a fixed sequence of six steps
segments.shown_as: a law-book icon with the IBC title, then a blue panel with a single line and six dots, each dot stemmed to a step chip; a black ring settles on the first dot as the first step is named

segments.teaches: step 1: a lender that cannot recover its loan files an insolvency application with NCLT (set up in 2016, the adjudicating authority for companies and LLPs, 16 branches); NCLT's order can be appealed to NCLAT, a High Court or the Supreme Court

elements.what: cream chip 'Admission of Insolvency Application'
bank building
arrow labelled 'Application' from the bank to the NCLT seal
round NCLT seal with the national emblem
paragraph under the seal: constituted 2016, adjudicating authority for insolvency of companies and LLPs under IBC
blue '16 Branches' badge under the seal
long arrow labelled 'appeal' to three higher bodies
NCLAT seal, a domed High Court building and the Supreme Court building, with NCLAT's full name under a dotted stem

segments.notes: 8 change events. The tribunal's units are usually called benches, shown as 'branches'. The High Court as an appeal forum needs checking (under the Code, appeals go to NCLAT and then the Supreme Court).
segments.idea: the lender starts the process by applying to a special tribunal, whose decision can be appealed higher up
segments.shown_as: the bank on the left sends an arrow labelled 'Application' into the NCLT seal; a '16 Branches' badge clips under the seal and a definition paragraph writes on beneath; then an 'appeal' arrow runs right to three higher bodies (NCLAT seal, High Court dome, Supreme Court building)

segments.teaches: back on the map: step 1 is done at NCLT; the applicant may withdraw the application within 30 days; the ring moves to step 2

elements.what: the six-dot CIRP map returns
'NCLT' label over the first dot
blue italic note under step 1: creditors can withdraw the application within 30 days
black ring slides from dot 1 to dot 2

segments.notes: The 30-day note appears at 95.4 s, about 5 s before it is spoken; the rule itself needs checking. The ring moves on 'next step' (106.6 s).
segments.idea: the map shows which body acts at step 1 and when the case moves on
segments.shown_as: the map returns with an 'NCLT' tag pinned on the first dot and a note under it about withdrawal; the black ring slides to the second dot as 'next step' is said

segments.teaches: step 2: once the case is admitted the company is headed for sale, so an insolvency professional takes charge of its affairs to keep up its value, and the lenders whose money is stuck form a committee of creditors

elements.what: two heading chips 'Committee of Creditors' and 'Insolvency professional'
bank building
arrow from bank to factory carrying a cream '10 Cr Loan' box under a red 'NPA' tag
black factory (the defaulting company)
dotted 'Payback' elbow from the factory back to the bank, red cross at the factory end
green dotted frame drawn round the factory
IP role under the frame: runs the company's affairs during CIRP and works to maximise asset value
curved arrow from the bank down to the 'Committee of Creditors' chip
CoC: financial creditors who lent to the distressed company

segments.notes: 7 change events. The chips start as headings and fly into the picture: IP into the factory frame (132 s), CoC to the bank (145.6 s, about 2.7 s before 'committee' is said). '10 Cr' and 'NPA' are never spoken. Neither the professional nor the creditors are drawn as people.
segments.idea: a defaulting company is handed to a professional manager, and its lenders band together to decide what happens to it
segments.shown_as: a bank lends '10 Cr' to a factory; the loan is tagged NPA and the dotted payback line back to the bank is crossed; a green frame is drawn round the factory and the 'Insolvency professional' chip flies from the heading into it, with its role written under it; then the 'Committee of Creditors' chip flies down beside the bank on a curved arrow, with its members written under it
segments.example: a 10 crore loan from a bank to a factory turned NPA (on screen only)

segments.teaches: back on the map: the ring moves to step 3, inviting resolution proposers

elements.what: the CIRP map with the NCLT tag on dot 1
black ring slides from dot 2 to dot 3

segments.notes: Navigation only; the ring lands about 1 s before 'resolution proposals' is said.
segments.idea: the case moves on to finding buyers
segments.shown_as: the map returns and the black ring slides to the third dot, 'Invite Resolution Proposers'

segments.teaches: step 3: potential investors who think they can turn the company around submit resolution plans to the committee of creditors; the committee picks one plan, and if members disagree the plan with the highest vote share wins

elements.what: cream chip 'Invite Resolution Proposers' top-left and a heading 'Resolution Proposers'
three cream chips 'Potential Investor 1/2/3'
three document icons in a blue column, one per investor, with dotted arrows from each investor
dotted arrows from the three documents converging on the 'Committee of Creditors' chip under a bank icon
blue notes: applicants submit plans to CoC; CoC may select any one; the plan with the highest vote share is taken up

segments.notes: The investors are text chips, not drawn people. Transcript gap 182.3-186.8 s, right after the bank and CoC appear; the 'applicants submit their plans' note (183.8 s) falls inside it. 'Highest vote share' is a simplification: the Code sets a minimum share of the creditors' vote for approval (worth checking).
segments.idea: many outside investors offer plans to rescue the company; the lenders choose one by vote
segments.shown_as: three investor chips on the right each pass a document along a dotted arrow; the three documents' arrows converge on the Committee of Creditors chip under a bank icon; blue notes write on below: any one plan may be chosen, by vote share
segments.example: three potential investors, one plan chosen

segments.teaches: who may not be a resolution applicant: undischarged insolvents, wilful defaulters, people convicted of offences carrying two or more years in jail, those whose own account has been NPA for over a year, and (after a 2017 amendment against misuse) promoters bidding for their own company

elements.what: black elbow line from the 'Resolution Proposers' heading up to a blue 'INELIGIBLE' band

five black-square bullets written one by one: undischarged insolvent; wilful defaulter; convicted of an offence with two or more years' imprisonment; account in NPA for 1+ year; promoter bidding for own company

segments.notes: 6 change events, each bullet on its spoken word except the NPA bullet (about 4 s early) and the promoter bullet (about 3 s early). From 240 s to 267 s the misuse story is told with no visual change.
segments.idea: the Code bars certain kinds of people from bidding for a distressed company, including its own defaulting promoters
segments.shown_as: an elbow line lifts from the 'Resolution Proposers' heading to an 'INELIGIBLE' band, and a list of five disqualifications writes on beneath it, one bullet per spoken item
segments.example: promoters who did not repay came back as bidders for their own company; barred by the 2017 amendment

segments.teaches: steps 4-6: NCLT approves the plan chosen by the committee, monitors its implementation, and the application is closed; the whole process is time-bound: 14 days to accept or reject the application, 330 days in all

segments.idea: the tribunal signs off the chosen plan and watches it through; the whole rescue has a fixed deadline
